episodes.167451: A dry-line/cold front was moving across Minnesota during the afternoon of Monday, May 9th. A few thunderstorms developed along this front across central Minnesota, and quickly spread south and eastward during the late afternoon and evening over eastern Minnesota, and adjacent west central Wisconsin. A brief funnel cloud was observed south of Gilman, and a tornado impacted Dakota County between Hastings and Miesville. Large hail and a few damaging wind gusts occurred along this line as it moved eastward. The largest hail stone was 2 inches in diameter and occurred near St. Paul downtown airport.
episodes.167452: A dry-line/cold front that spawn a couple of tornadoes in eastern Minnesota, moved across west central Wisconsin during the evening and produced an additional three tornadoes, plus wind damage, and large hail. The tornadoes occurred near Lake Pepin, near Knapp, and between Colfax and Elk Mound in Dunn County.
episodes.167756: An unseasonal cold upper-level trough and associated front moved through Northwest California. The system brought lower snow levels and post-frontal hail showers. Small hail covered roadways caused a couple of accidents.
episodes.167906: Widespread severe thunderstorms developed on the afternoon of the tenth as a weak upper level disturbance ejected overhead northward out of Mexico. The initial activity rapidly developed near the dryline, which was located near the Texas/New Mexico line, late Tuesday afternoon. Aided by strong instability, several of the storms quickly became severe mostly producing severe thunderstorm winds. The thunderstorms gradually evolved into a solid line and tracked eastward across much of the South Plains, Rolling Plains and southern Texas Panhandle through the mid-late evening hours continually producing severe winds. Lastly, a wake low developed in the departing convection which generated a high wind gust of 62 mph near McAdoo measured by the Texas Tech University West Texas mesonet.
episodes.167923: A line of strong to severe thunderstorms developed across western Wisconsin ahead of an approaching warm front, then tracked through central Wisconsin during the late evening hours on Monday (5/9).  The strongest storms produced isolated large hail up to ping pong size across portions of central Wisconsin before diminishing through the overnight hours.
episodes.167924: Strong to severe storms developed during the late afternoon and early evening hours on Tuesday (5/10) across north-central and far northeast Wisconsin.  The strongest storms produced hail up to 2 inches in diameter.
episodes.168261: Heavy rain generated flooding along the Little Minnesota River near Peever. Flood stage was exceeded on May 10 at 17.69 feet but fell below flood stage on May 11 in the early morning hours. Impacts from this flood event are unknown.
episodes.168749: An upper level ridge was centered over the Texas Coast with an upper-low pressure system over Northern California. A dryline was across portions of Southeast New Mexico and West Texas. High moisture and instability were present to the east of the dryline. Wind shear was moderate, and an upper level disturbance moved over the area which provided additional lift. These conditions resulted in thunderstorms that produced large hail, strong winds, and flash flooding across portions of West Texas.
episodes.169262: A line of storms moved across southeast Minnesota during the evening of May 9th. These storms produced hail across portions of Wabasha and Olmsted Counties. The largest reported hail was half dollar sized in Lake City (Wabasha County). A few strong wind gusts also occurred and the automated weather observing equipment at the Rochester (Olmsted County) airport measured a 76 mph gust.
episodes.169282: Thunderstorms developing along a frontal boundary turned severe, forming large hail over portions of central Upper Michigan during the late afternoon and evening of the 10th.
episodes.169302: A line of storms moved across portions of northeast Iowa during the evening of May 9th. These storms produced some hail with up to golf ball sized reported near Mitchell (Mitchell County).
episodes.169304: A line of storms moved across portions of western Wisconsin during the evening of May 9th. These storms produced some hail and the largest reported was quarter sized north of Holmen (La Crosse County).
episodes.169507: An isolated severe thunderstorm produced up to one inch diameter hail.
episodes.169703: An upper level system over northern California ushered mid-level moisture into West Texas, with a weak disturbance aloft assisting in shower and thunderstorm development across the Texas and Oklahoma Panhandles. A dryline stretched southwest to northeast across the central Texas Panhandle with strong to severe scattered thunderstorms initiating along and east of the dryline during the late afternoon hours. Large hail up to tennis ball size and wind gusts up to 60 to 70 mph with some areas of blowing dust were reported throughout the late afternoon and early evening hours. By sunset, the storms became linear and wind driven with a decreasing threat of hail but a continuation of severe wind gusts up to 70 to 80 mph. The highest wind gust of 81 mph was measured at the West Texas Mesonet 2 miles east of Pampa, Texas. Following the line of storms, light rain showers developed with bursts of gusty winds across portions of the eastern half of the Texas and Oklahoma Panhandles. In addition, a few non-thunderstorm severe wind gusts also occurred on the western edge of the light precipitation prior to all severe wind reports ending before Midnight.
episodes.169809: A few thunderstorms developing along a frontal boundary turned strong to severe over Lake Superior during the late afternoon and evening of the 10th.
episodes.170065: Spring snowmelt, record April precipitation and frequent May rain events led to strong hydrologic responses within the Rainy Lake basin. Namakan Lake, Kabetogama Lake and Rainy Lake rose above the flood of record during the months of May and June before subsiding in July and returning to levels closer to normal. These high lake levels led to significant damage to homes and businesses along the shoreline along with docks and other related structures. Additionally, some roads were covered in water with one being temporarily raised to maintain access to a few resorts. In addition to the costs of the damage itself, many resorts in the area suffered from lost revenue by having to close during the beginning of peak tourist season in the area.
episodes.170374: An ice jam formed in the Yukon River approximately 6 miles down river of Circle causing flooding.

events.narrative: The starting point was estimated based on video evidence as it began over the Mississippi River (Lake Pepin). Once onshore, the tornado knocked down or broke about one dozen trees as it moved up the river bluffs and dissipated. Maximum winds were estimated at 70 mph.
Quarter sized hail was reported north of Oak Center.
Numerous trees were broken, including at a homestead east of Knapp. Maximum winds were estimated at 80 mph.
Up to half dollar sized hail was reported in Lake City.

Tornado began just north of I-94 near Rusk. The damage continued through Whitetail Golf Course. An irrigation system was tipped over, an outbuilding was torn apart, a trailer tipped over, and hundreds of trees were uprooted or snapped. Although the maximum wind speed was estimated at 90 mph, at times the winds were not as strong as 90 mph.
The automated weather observing equipment at the Rochester airport measured a 76 mph wind gust.
A 60 mph wind gust occurred in Millville.
Ping pong ball sized hail was reported in Osage.

An ice jam formed the evening of May 9th in that Yukon River which caused flooding in the village of Circle. This flooding caused the road to the airport to the airport to become impassable. The Steese Highway was flooded  with 12 inches of water. The high water levels caused the community well to flood requiring the well to be disinfected before it could be used again. One home had water enter the bottom floor.
Golf ball sized hail was reported northeast of Mitchell.
There was a report of a funnel cloud southeast of Eau Claire.
Quarter sized hail fell north of Holmen.
Quarter size hail fell in Plover.

Up to one inch diameter hail was reported across portions of Ionia county late in the evening.

Above normal snowfall for the 2021-2022 season was observed across northern portions of Koochiching and St. Louis counties and much of that remained on the ground into April. Heavy rainfall then fell on top of that above normal snowpack at the end of April and sent abnormally high amounts of runoff into the Rainy River Basin leading to rises on Namakan Lake and Kabetogama Lake. International Falls experienced their wettest April on record, helping to set the stage for the flooding. By the end of May, the level of Rainy Lake reached 1112.4 feet which was 12 inches above the 2014 peak level and 7 inches below the all-time record set in 1950. The high lake levels led to extensive damage to properties adjacent to the water along with damage to docks and other infrastructure. Lake levels would continue to rise into June.

Above normal snowfall for the 2021-2022 season was observed across northern portions of Koochiching and St. Louis counties and much of that remained on the ground into April. Heavy rainfall then fell on top of that above normal snowpack at the end of April and sent abnormally high amounts of runoff into the Rainy River Basin leading to rises on Rainy Lake. International Falls experienced their wettest April on record, helping to set the stage for the flooding. By the end of May, the level of Rainy Lake reached 1112.4 feet which was 12 inches above the 2014 peak level and 7 inches below the all-time record set in 1950. The level of Namakan Lake and Kabatogama Lake reached 1122.2 feet which was 20.5 inches above the 2014 peak level and 7 inches below the all-time record set in 1916. The high lake levels led to extensive damage to properties adjacent to the water along with damage to docks and other infrastructure. Lake levels would continue to rise into June.

A thunderstorm moved across Pecos County and produced wind damage in Fort Stockton. There were multiple trees uprooted, leaning power poles, snapped power lines, and peeled or separated roofs at several homes, apartment buildings, and businesses on the south side of Fort Stockton. The storm survey results estimated peak wind speeds to be between 70 to 80 mph. The cost of damage is a very rough estimate.
